page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical execution cores across 2 threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI.

The server does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block volumes. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. In standard benchmarking, single-core and multi-core computational throughput via stress-ng registers at 1305.28 and 3458.1, placing CPU capacity in the lower quartile relative to broader cloud standards. Memory subsystem evaluation via PassMark yields 1902.06, reflecting average performance for this tier, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidth reaching 25.47 GB/sec and 22.43 GB/sec respectively.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance offers consistent dedicated compute resources rather than burstable allocations, but its overall compute density and processing speed remain modest. Static web serving throughput reaches 3.54 GB/sec, and in-memory operations measure 3.37 million Redis SET operations per second. Given the lack of local NVMe storage and entry-level compute metrics, the ecs.g6.xlarge is best suited for general-purpose application hosting, microservices, light relational databases, staging environments, and intermediate caching layers that do not demand high I/O or sustained compute intensity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it features hardware support for AVX-512 instructions but lacks integrated local disk storage and GPU hardware. Network throughput is baselined at 2 Gbps. Across benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers entry-level compute scores, achieving 1156.0 single-core and 2546.0 multi-core points in Geekbench, alongside an average PassMark memory score of 1902.06. Memory read bandwidth reaches 25.47 GB/sec for uncached blocks. The balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory configuration provides stable resource allocation suitable for standard web serving, containerized services, microservices, background job workers, and development testing environments.
